findings.title: Queries are now interpolated repeatedly (shard path 3x, normal split path 2x)
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, filters)` on every target. `runShardSplitQuery` already interpolates its targets (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52). It then calls `runSplitQuery` once per shard group, which interpolates the already-interpolated targets again. Each sub-request then goes through `datasource.runQuery`, which (as `DataSourceWithBackend.query`) interpolates a third time. On the plain split path interpolation also happens twice, where before it happened once. `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent. Ad-hoc filters (`request.filters`) can be injected into the expression more than once. Variable values that were already substituted and contain `$name`-like text get re-interpolated. Interpolation should happen once at the entry point. The shard path should hand already-interpolated targets to an inner function that skips interpolation, or `runSplitQuery` should skip it when called from the shard path.

findings.title: Test locks in redundant repeated interpolation as expected behaviour
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (1 call from the shard entry plus 4 from the per-shard `runSplitQuery` sub-requests) asserts the double interpolation as correct. The count depends on the number of shard groups, so it breaks whenever the shard grouping changes. If interpolation is later de-duplicated, this test fails for the wrong reason. The test should assert that the interpolated query reaches `runQuery`, or that interpolation happens once per user query, not an exact call count. The `applyTemplateVariables` mocks also mutate and return the input query in place, which hides any bugs from repeated application on the same object.
